title: "Post-aggregation analysis"
output: html_document

```{r, load-data}
set.seed(getOption("EpiATLAS_AS_SEED", 42L))

# Per-filter invocation (PLAN §4.12e per-filter incremental outputs): 05 builds
# one transcript_filter per run from that filter's upstream outputs and writes
# aggregated_dt_filtered_{tf}.csv.gz. Snakemake passes TRANSCRIPT_FILTER;
# interactive runs fall back to the YAML param / primary filter.
this_transcript_filter <- Sys.getenv(
  "TRANSCRIPT_FILTER",
  getOption("EpiATLAS_AS_PRIMARY_FILTER", "biotype_filtered")
)
tf <- this_transcript_filter

keep_rows_manual <- readRDS(
  sprintf("processed_data/keep_rows_manual_%s.rds", tf)
)
file_metadata <- fread("processed_data/file_table.csv.gz")
metadata <- fread(sample_metadata_file)
event_annotations_dt <- fread(
  sprintf("processed_data/event_annotations_dt_%s.csv.gz", tf)
)
psi_long_dt <- fread(sprintf("processed_data/psi_long_dt_%s.csv.gz", tf))
ijc_sjc_dt <- fread(sprintf("processed_data/ijc_sjc_dt_%s.csv.gz", tf))
# locate per-filter ChIP aggregation outputs (sample_dts/chip_agg_{tf}/)
chip_agg_dir <- file.path(sample_dt_dir, sprintf("chip_agg_%s", tf))
file_metadata[,
  local_file := file.path(chip_agg_dir, paste0(basename(file_path), ".tab.gz"))
]
# Every ChIP metadata entry MUST have an aggregated tab. ALL ChIP source bigwigs
# exist on disk — observed (…pval.signal.bigwig) AND ChromImpute imputed
# (impute_*.pval.bw) — so a missing .tab.gz means the aggregation is INCOMPLETE
# (a bug: e.g. the CHIP_BW glob once missed all 135 imputed tracks). Fail hard
# with the count + an example — do NOT silently proceed on a subset (that masks
# the bug + drops real data). Genuine no-data cohorts (AMED-CREST RNA) don't
# apply here; every ChIP file_path resolves.
.missing_chip <- file_metadata[
  assay_type == "ChIP-Seq" & !file.exists(local_file)
]
if (nrow(.missing_chip) > 0L) {
  stop(sprintf(
    "ChIP aggregation INCOMPLETE: %d/%d tabs missing. First missing: %s (source exists: %s). Check the aggregate_chip_one/aggregate_chip_imp globs.",
    nrow(.missing_chip),
    file_metadata[assay_type == "ChIP-Seq", .N],
    .missing_chip$local_file[1],
    file.exists(file.path(
      "/nfs/data3/IHEC/ChIP-Seq",
      basename(.missing_chip$file_path[1])
    ))
  ))
}

# # we only need ChIP-Seq data, since WGBS has been aggregated via the matrices
# file_table <- file_table[assay_type == "ChIP-Seq"]

# load WGBS data (per-filter)
wgbs_agg <- fread(file.path(sample_dt_dir, sprintf("WGBS_agg_%s.csv.gz", tf)))
wgbs_agg <- wgbs_agg[!startsWith(name, "chromhmm")]
wgbs_agg <- melt(
  wgbs_agg,
  id.vars = c("ID", "ihec", "name"),
  value.name = "score",
  variable.name = "experiment_type",
  measure.vars = c("score", "n")
)
wgbs_agg[experiment_type == "score", experiment_type := "DNAm"]
wgbs_agg[experiment_type == "n", experiment_type := "CpGs"]

wgbs_agg[, ihec := sub("\\.[0-9]+$", "", ihec)]

# bind all the samples for the histone marks
#
# Memory note: at full scale this table is ~1.03e9 rows (2430 files x
# ~424k windows), so column choices matter a lot here. bigWigAverageOverBed
# emits 8 columns (name size covered sum mean0 mean min max); only `name`
# (window id) and `mean` are ever used downstream (everything else is
# discarded before the dcast a few lines below and nothing later re-reads
# it) — keeping all 8 would cost ~40 bytes/row x 1.03e9 rows =~ 41 GB for
# columns that are immediately dropped. `select=` at fread() time avoids
# ever allocating them. Likewise, attaching `ihec`/`experiment_type` per
# file here (instead of carrying the full `local_file` path column through
# the whole long table, as before) saves another ~8 GB of pure pointer
# overhead for a value only ever used to look these two up.
chip_files <- file_metadata[assay_type == "ChIP-Seq"]
histone_dt <- rbindlist(
  pbmcapply::pbmcmapply(
    FUN = function(file, this_ihec, this_mark) {
      dt <- fread(file, select = c(1, 6), col.names = c("name", "score"))
      dt <- dt[!startsWith(name, "chromhmm")]
      dt[, ihec := this_ihec]
      dt[, experiment_type := this_mark]
      dt
    },
    file = chip_files$local_file,
    this_ihec = chip_files$epirr_id_without_version,
    this_mark = chip_files$experiment_type,
    SIMPLIFY = FALSE
  )
)

# find common cols and rows
common_ihec <- intersect(histone_dt[, unique(ihec)], wgbs_agg[, unique(ihec)])
common_cols <- intersect(names(histone_dt), names(wgbs_agg))
```


```{r, build-aggregated-dt}
# bind histone and WGBS data
message("Building aggregated feature table from histone and WGBS inputs...")
aggregated_dt <- rbindlist(list(
  histone_dt[ihec %in% common_ihec, ..common_cols],
  wgbs_agg[ihec %in% common_ihec, ..common_cols]
))
# histone_dt (~30G, the ~1e9-row ChIP long table) and wgbs_agg are not used
# after this rbind — free them before the tstrsplit + dcast, which otherwise
# hold their working copies ON TOP of these (the chunk-4 OOM peak was 98G).
rm(histone_dt, wgbs_agg)
gc()

# some data wrangling to prepare the data for putting into wide format
aggregated_dt[, c("position", "ID") := tstrsplit(name, "_", fixed = TRUE)]
# there is an ID for all of them, so remove this line
# aggregated_dt[is.na(ID), c("position", "ID"):=list('event_name', position)]
# aggregated_dt[position=="up", position:="upstream_other_region"]
# aggregated_dt[position=="down", position:="downstream_other_region"]
aggregated_dt[, experiment_type := droplevels(experiment_type)]
aggregated_dt[, ihec := as.factor(ihec)]
aggregated_dt[, ID := as.integer(ID)]
# from long to wide
message("Casting long-format measurements to wide format...")
aggregated_dt <- dcast(
  aggregated_dt,
  ihec + ID ~ experiment_type + position,
  value.var = "score",
  sep = ";"
)
setnames(aggregated_dt, old = "ihec", new = "IHEC")

# §4.13l — per-mark observed/imputed source covariate. 04-2-chip-signal-sanity
# found imputed ChIP tracks run 1.7-7x higher median signal than observed for
# every mark (worst for H3K27me3/H3K9me3), and this status is per (sample,
# mark) — a sample can have some marks observed and others imputed — so it
# is NOT captured by anything already in aggregated_dt. Derived directly
# from chip_files (a per-file property, constant across all windows for a
# mark) rather than carried through the window-level table.
#
# Written as a STRING ("observed"/"imputed"), not a 0/1 flag, so it is
# auto-routed to the categorical/nominal branch of both downstream
# pipelines without any code changes there: splicing_ml's
# infer_feature_columns() buckets by dtype (non-numeric -> categorical_cols
# -> OneHotEncoder, same as `protocol`); 09zz-ml-event-glmnet-tidymodels.R's
# tidymodels recipe uses all_nominal_predictors() -> step_dummy(). A numeric
# 0/1 encoding would risk being misclassified as a continuous histone
# signal by splicing_ml's `col.startswith("H3K")` clip-column rule if named
# with an H3K prefix; the `_source` suffix and string dtype sidestep this
# even though the column also happens to start with "H3K".
chip_source <- unique(chip_files[, .(
  IHEC = epirr_id_without_version,
  mark = experiment_type,
  source = fifelse(uuid == "imputed", "imputed", "observed")
)])
chip_source_wide <- dcast(chip_source, IHEC ~ mark, value.var = "source")
source_cols <- setdiff(names(chip_source_wide), "IHEC")
setnames(
  chip_source_wide,
  old = source_cols,
  new = paste0(source_cols, "_source")
)
source_cols <- paste0(source_cols, "_source")

aggregated_dt[
  chip_source_wide,
  on = "IHEC",
  (source_cols) := mget(paste0("i.", source_cols))
]

# write full table to disk
message("Writing processed_data/aggregated_dt.csv.gz...")
fwrite(aggregated_dt, "processed_data/aggregated_dt.csv.gz")
```


```{r, chip-signal-sanity}
# §4.13b — ChIP signal assertion: NA fraction < 5% and non-negative, for
# observed (non-imputed) samples only. Imputed samples may have higher NA.
observed_ihec <- file_metadata[
  assay_type == "ChIP-Seq" & uuid != "imputed",
  unique(epirr_id_without_version)
]
chip_marks <- file_metadata[assay_type == "ChIP-Seq", unique(experiment_type)]
chip_cols <- grep(
  paste0("^(", paste(chip_marks, collapse = "|"), ");"),
  names(aggregated_dt),
  value = TRUE
)
observed_dt <- aggregated_dt[IHEC %in% observed_ihec]
for (col in chip_cols) {
  vals <- observed_dt[[col]]
  na_frac <- mean(is.na(vals))
  stopifnot(na_frac < 0.05)
  stopifnot(all(vals[!is.na(vals)] >= 0))
}
```


```{r, melt-psi}
# psi_long_dt from 03 is already long format (ID, uuid, psi) — no melt needed
melted_psi <- copy(psi_long_dt)
setnames(melted_psi, "psi", "PSI")
melted_psi[
  event_annotations_dt,
  on = .(ID),
  c("Event Type", "transcript_filter", "gene_id") := .(
    `Event Type`,
    transcript_filter,
    gene_id
  )
]
melted_psi <- melted_psi[!is.na(PSI)]
melted_psi[file_metadata, on = .(uuid), IHEC := epirr_id_without_version]
```


```{r, expand-aggregated-dt}
# guard against re-running this chunk on an already-expanded aggregated_dt
# (merge() would silently produce PSI.x/PSI.y instead of erroring clearly).
# If this trips, reload the cheap checkpoint instead of rerunning
# build-aggregated-dt: aggregated_dt <- fread("processed_data/aggregated_dt.csv.gz")
stopifnot(!("PSI" %in% names(aggregated_dt)))

# merge PSI on the aggregated table
aggregated_dt <- merge(
  aggregated_dt,
  melted_psi[
    ID %in% keep_rows_manual & !is.na(PSI),
    .(ID, IHEC, uuid, PSI, transcript_filter)
  ],
  by = c("ID", "IHEC")
)
# remove NA PSIs
aggregated_dt <- aggregated_dt[!is.na(PSI)]

# §4.8 — carry junction read counts (IJC/SJC) forward from 03. Needed
# downstream for coverage-weighted model fitting (sample_weight = IJC + SJC)
# and beta-binomial regression on raw counts, and here for the §4.13i
# coverage sanity check. Joined on (ID, uuid) — same keys as psi_long_dt.
aggregated_dt[
  ijc_sjc_dt,
  on = .(ID, uuid),
  c("IJC", "SJC") := .(i.IJC, i.SJC)
]

# NA for columns starting with CpGs can be replaced by 0, because NA means no CpGs were covered in that window, which is equivalent to 0.
for (i in grep("^CpGs", names(aggregated_dt))) {
  set(aggregated_dt, i = which(is.na(aggregated_dt[[i]])), j = i, value = 0)
}

# gather the intrinsic features
# Note: splice-site scores (3ss, 5ss, etc.) joined separately after MaxEntScan rule
cols_to_add <- c(
  "distance_TSS",
  "distance_TES",
  "distance_gene_start",
  "distance_gene_end",
  "width;upstream_other_region",
  "width;event_name",
  "width;downstream_other_region",
  "Event Type",
  "gene_id",
  "seqnames",
  "Variability"
)

# add the intrinsic features
aggregated_dt[
  event_annotations_dt,
  on = .(ID),
  (cols_to_add) := mget(cols_to_add)
]

# --- DROP events with uncomputable Variability (NA sd_psi) --------------------
# NA Variability == NA sd_psi == <2 non-NA PSI samples after the 02-3 masking:
# such events cannot be classified (median split) or used cross-sample, and are
# unusable in 06 correlation + 09-1 (minimum_events guard) + any variability
# stratification; contribution to the pooled splicing_ml is <=1 row each
# (negligible, and biotype_filtered's `both` config is excluded anyway). Drop
# here so aggregated_dt_filtered is clean for ALL consumers.
# FIXED upstream 2026-07-13: 03's keep_rows_manual now includes
# `!is.na(sd_psi)`, so a fresh 03 rerun will no longer emit these ~317 events
# at all. This block is now defense-in-depth (kept in place so already-cached
# 03/04 outputs from before that fix, or a stale keep_rows_manual_{tf}.rds, are
# still handled correctly) rather than the primary filter. Until every
# transcript_filter's 03 output has actually been regenerated,
# keep_rows_manual_{tf}.rds may still be a SUPERSET of the modelled set —
# direct readers (09-1/10) must intersect with aggregated_dt IDs.
# NB Variability is CHARACTER and the NA-sd_psi events come through as EMPTY
# STRING "", not NA: 03 fwrite writes NA-char as "" and fread reads it back as ""
# (default na.strings = "NA", not ""). So test both is.na() AND == "".
.na_var <- is.na(aggregated_dt$Variability) | aggregated_dt$Variability == ""
n_na_variability_dropped <- aggregated_dt[.na_var, uniqueN(ID)]
if (n_na_variability_dropped > 0L) {
  warning(sprintf(
    "05: dropping %d events with unset Variability (NA/'' == <2 valid PSI samples, sd_psi undefined) - now also filtered upstream in 03 keep_rows_manual as of 2026-07-13; this is a defense-in-depth catch for outputs from before that fix.",
    n_na_variability_dropped
  ))
  aggregated_dt <- aggregated_dt[!(is.na(Variability) | Variability == "")]
}

# also add the protocol
aggregated_dt[file_metadata, on = .(uuid), protocol := experiment_type]
# add the ontology term and the project
aggregated_dt[
  metadata,
  on = c(IHEC = "epirr_id_without_version"),
  c("ontology", "project") := .(
    factor(harmonized_sample_ontology_term_high_order_fig1),
    factor(project)
  )
]

# §2.1 — QC flag count covariate, joined by uuid (NOT epirr_id_without_version:
# epirrs with both mRNA-Seq + total-RNA-Seq have multiple uuids). No samples
# dropped; all 405 epirrs retained.
qc_flag_covariates <- fread("processed_data/qc_flag_covariates.csv")
aggregated_dt[
  qc_flag_covariates,
  on = .(uuid),
  qc_flag_count := i.qc_flag_count
]


# # load transcript ids per filter
# filtered_transcript_ids <- readRDS(
#   "splicing_analysis/filtered_transcript_ids.rds"
# )
# # `transcript_filters` was previously an undefined variable here (only
# # worked by accident if a prior interactive session had it in the global
# # env, e.g. from running 03 first) — derive it from the actual upstream
# # artifact instead of hardcoding a second copy of the three filter names.
# transcript_filters <- names(filtered_transcript_ids)

### Old implementation recomputed TPM, now that we have §4.12b, we use the lengthScaledTPM + vst from 04-5-rnaseq-normalisation.Rmd
# # load isoform quantifications
# isoform_quants <- fread(
#   "splicing_analysis/isoform_quantifications_subset.tsv.gz"
# )
# # compute gene-level quantifications
# gene_quants <- rbindlist(
#   sapply(
#     transcript_filters,
#     function(this_transcript_filter) {
#       # subset the isoform quantifications to the samples we want to use
#       this_filtered_transcripts <- filtered_transcript_ids[[
#         this_transcript_filter
#       ]]

#       # filter the isoform quantifications to the filtered transcripts and compute gene-level quantifications by summing the TPMs of the transcripts per gene
#       isoform_quants_filtered <- copy(isoform_quants[
#         transcript_id %in% this_filtered_transcripts
#       ])
#       isoform_quants_filtered[
#         effective_length > 0,
#         RPK := 1000 * expected_count / effective_length,
#         by = .(uuid, epirr_id_without_version)
#       ]
#       isoform_quants_filtered[,
#         TPM_rec := 1000000 * RPK / sum(RPK, na.rm = TRUE),
#         by = .(uuid, epirr_id_without_version)
#       ]
#       isoform_quants_filtered[is.na(TPM_rec), TPM_rec := 0]
#       isoform_quants_filtered[,
#         TPM_scale := 1000000 * TPM / sum(TPM, na.rm = TRUE),
#         .(uuid, epirr_id_without_version)
#       ]
#     },
#     simplify = FALSE
#   ),
#   idcol = "transcript_filter"
# )
# # manually change gene_id for ENSG00000213593.9_and_ENSG00000254462.1_and_ENSG00000211450.9_and_ENSG00000198561.13 from the manual ids that were kept
# # aggregated_dt[gene_id == "ENSG00000213593.9_and_ENSG00000254462.1_and_ENSG00000211450.9_and_ENSG00000198561.13", gene_id := "ENSG00000198561.13"]
# # §4.12a — gene_quants is at transcript level (one row per transcript per
# # sample); aggregate to gene level before joining, otherwise data.table's
# # last-write-wins `:=` join picks an arbitrary single transcript's TPM_scale
# # instead of the gene-level sum across all transcripts.
# gene_quants_agg <- gene_quants[,
#   .(gene_expression = sum(TPM_scale, na.rm = TRUE)),
#   by = .(transcript_filter, uuid, gene_id)
# ]

gene_quants_agg <- fread(
  sprintf("processed_data/gene_expression_normalised_%s.csv.gz", tf)
)

# §4.12b — keep BOTH normalised representations under explicit names; there
# is deliberately no ambiguous `gene_expression` column. Consumers pick by
# column structure (see revision/PLAN.md §4.12b, file-changes specs):
#   - gene_expression_getmm : GeTMM-CPM, length- AND composition-corrected,
#     cross-gene comparable WITHOUT per-gene z-scoring. Use where the feature
#     is one column with many different host genes stacked in the rows and no
#     per-gene rescaling happens -> the genome-wide pooled table
#     (splicing_ml). Also the correct scale for any raw >=0 / log1p / ==0 /
#     threshold check (the §4.12e mask uses it below).
#   - gene_expression_vst : DESeq2 vst, variance-stabilised, cross-SAMPLE
#     comparable only (NOT length-corrected). Use where each column is a
#     single gene varying across samples and gets z-scored per column anyway
#     -> event-specific models (07/09) and every RBP expression column.
#     Roughly log2-scale, CAN BE NEGATIVE: never apply log1p/log to it.
aggregated_dt[
  gene_quants_agg,
  on = .(transcript_filter, uuid, gene_id),
  c("gene_expression_vst", "gene_expression_getmm") := .(
    i.gene_expression_vst,
    i.gene_expression_getmm
  )
]

# §3.4 / §4.12f — RBP + core-spliceosome expression features (from 04-6, all on
# gene_expression_vst: single-gene columns, same routing as host expression).
# rbp_score_* : per (ID, uuid), sum/mean/max expression of the RBPs with a
# binding site near the event (binding-site-filtered). Events with no nearby RBP
# get no row -> impute 0, NOT the column mean: 0 correctly encodes "no local RBP
# signal"; the mean would fabricate a nonzero regulator score.
rbp_score_dt <- fread(sprintf("processed_data/rbp_score_dt_%s.csv.gz", tf))
aggregated_dt[
  rbp_score_dt,
  on = .(ID, uuid, transcript_filter),
  c("rbp_score_sum", "rbp_score_mean", "rbp_score_max", "rbp_n") := .(
    i.rbp_score_sum,
    i.rbp_score_mean,
    i.rbp_score_max,
    i.rbp_n
  )
]
# rbp_n (# distinct expressed RBPs near the event) rides alongside so the model
# can separate "how many RBPs" from "how much each" — rbp_score_sum conflates
# them (see 04-6 Step 2a). Events with no nearby RBP get 0 (real value), not mean.
for (col in c("rbp_score_sum", "rbp_score_mean", "rbp_score_max", "rbp_n")) {
  set(aggregated_dt, which(is.na(aggregated_dt[[col]])), col, 0)
}

# spliceosome_* : core-machinery expression, per (uuid) genome-wide (not
# site-filtered), joined on (uuid, transcript_filter). Present for every sample
# -> no imputation needed. Own prefix keeps "general machinery" separable from
# the local-regulator rbp_score_* in coefficient/importance output.
splicing_factor_expression <- fread(sprintf(
  "processed_data/splicing_factor_expression_%s.csv.gz",
  tf
))
spliceosome_cols <- setdiff(
  names(splicing_factor_expression),
  c("uuid", "transcript_filter")
)
aggregated_dt[
  splicing_factor_expression,
  on = .(uuid, transcript_filter),
  (spliceosome_cols) := mget(paste0("i.", spliceosome_cols))
]

# §5.12f sanity — rbp_score_*/rbp_n are 0-imputed above (real value, not
# missing), so must be non-NA for every row. spliceosome_* is joined
# genome-wide/unfiltered (every uuid has core-machinery expression), so must
# also be non-NA for ~100% of rows; any NA there means the (uuid,
# transcript_filter) join key didn't match splicing_factor_expression.
rbp_na_frac <- aggregated_dt[,
  mean(is.na(rbp_score_sum) | is.na(rbp_score_mean) | is.na(rbp_score_max) | is.na(rbp_n))
]
append_sanity(
  sprintf("rbp_score_non_na_%s", tf),
  ifelse(rbp_na_frac == 0, "PASS", "FAIL"),
  rbp_na_frac, 0,
  "rbp_score_sum/mean/max/rbp_n should be 0-imputed, never NA, after the §5.12f join"
)
spliceosome_na_frac <- aggregated_dt[,
  mean(rowSums(is.na(.SD)) > 0), .SDcols = spliceosome_cols
]
append_sanity(
  sprintf("spliceosome_non_na_%s", tf),
  ifelse(spliceosome_na_frac < 0.01, "PASS", "WARN"),
  spliceosome_na_frac, 0.01,
  "fraction of rows with >=1 NA spliceosome_* column (unfiltered genome-wide join, expect ~0)"
)

# §4.12e — the low-expression event filter is now applied UPSTREAM in
# 02-3-rmats-event-filtering.Rmd (per-(event,sample) expr_pass = VST host-gene
# gate AND per-cell read-coverage floor IJC+SJC>=min_read_coverage) and the
# minimum-sample floor was removed at data-construction. 05 therefore no longer
# masks PSI or drops events on expression/sample-count grounds — it only checks
# that the upstream gates held (see gene-expression-sanity + junction-coverage-
# sanity chunks). Masked cells were written NA in the .psi and already dropped
# above (aggregated_dt[!is.na(PSI)]).

# make sure all of the gene_expression values are at least one: (deprecated because we don't have the suppa tpm filter anymore)
# stopifnot(all(aggregated_dt[, gene_expression >= 1]))
# log the expression, we do that later

# remove the gene_id version
aggregated_dt[, gene_id := gsub(pattern = ".\\d+$", "", gene_id)]
```

```{r, gene-expression-sanity}
# §4.13d — gene expression distribution sanity (post §4.12a fix)
sanity_csv <- "qc/sanity_summary.csv"
append_sanity <- function(check_name, status, value, threshold, notes = "") {
  new_row <- data.table(
    check_name = check_name,
    status = status,
    value = value,
    threshold = threshold,
    notes = notes
  )
  if (file.exists(sanity_csv)) {
    # upsert by check_name: drop any prior row for this check before writing
    # the new one, so sanity_summary.csv doesn't accumulate stale/duplicate
    # rows across reruns (append=TRUE never truncated -> the file only grew).
    existing <- fread(sanity_csv)
    existing <- existing[check_name != new_row$check_name]
    fwrite(rbind(existing, new_row, fill = TRUE), sanity_csv)
  } else {
    fwrite(new_row, sanity_csv)
  }
}

dir.create("qc/distributions", recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

# record the NA-Variability drop (done above in expand-aggregated-dt); fixed
# upstream in 03 keep_rows_manual as of 2026-07-13 — this stays PASS/0 once
# every transcript_filter's 03 output has been regenerated.
append_sanity(
  sprintf("dropped_na_variability_events_%s", tf),
  if (n_na_variability_dropped > 0L) "WARN" else "PASS",
  n_na_variability_dropped, 0,
  "events dropped in 05 for NA Variability (<2 valid PSI samples, sd_psi undefined); now also filtered upstream in 03 keep_rows_manual (defense-in-depth here)"
)

# 1. log1p(gene_expression_getmm) boxplot by protocol
# getmm (CPM-like, >= 0) is the log1p-safe representation; vst can be
# negative and would produce NaNs under log().
p_gene_expr <- ggplot(
  unique(aggregated_dt[, .(uuid, protocol, gene_expression_getmm)]),
  aes(x = protocol, y = log1p(gene_expression_getmm))
) +
  geom_violin() +
  geom_boxplot(width = 0.5) +
  labs(
    title = "log1p(gene_expression_getmm) by protocol",
    x = "protocol",
    y = "log1p(gene_expression_getmm)"
  )
print(p_gene_expr)
ggsave(
  "qc/distributions/gene_expression_by_protocol.pdf",
  p_gene_expr,
  width = 7,
  height = 5
)

# (The old §4.12a cross-transcript_filter rank-correlation check was removed:
# 05 is now per-filter, so a single filter is present and the check is
# undefined. The §4.12a bug it guarded is moot anyway — gene_expression now
# comes from 02-2's normalised output, not the last-write-wins transcript join.)

# 2. % zero-expression events per sample (getmm: CPM-like, can be exactly 0;
# vst never is, so == 0 is only meaningful on getmm)
zero_frac_by_sample <- aggregated_dt[,
  .(zero_frac = mean(gene_expression_getmm == 0, na.rm = TRUE)),
  by = uuid
]
pct_over_thresh <- zero_frac_by_sample[, mean(zero_frac >= 0.30)]
append_sanity(
  "gene_expression_zero_frac_per_sample",
  ifelse(pct_over_thresh < 0.30, "PASS", "WARN"),
  pct_over_thresh,
  0.30,
  "fraction of samples with >=30% zero-expression events"
)

# §4.13d item 4 — housekeeping-gene cross-sample CV sanity. GAPDH/ACTB should
# be stably expressed across all 405 epirrs; a high CV would flag a
# normalisation problem. Sourced from `gene_quants_agg` (genome-wide,
# per-transcript_filter, built above for the §4.12b join) rather than
# `aggregated_dt`, because aggregated_dt is event-restricted — GAPDH/ACTB
# would only appear there if one of them happens to host a modelled AS event.
# getmm (CPM-like, >=0) is used, same convention as the other checks in this
# chunk (vst can cross zero, making sd/mean CV ill-defined).
housekeeping_ids <- c(GAPDH = "ENSG00000111640", ACTB = "ENSG00000075624")
for (hk_symbol in names(housekeeping_ids)) {
  hk_id <- housekeeping_ids[[hk_symbol]]
  hk_vals <- gene_quants_agg[gene_id == hk_id, gene_expression_getmm]
  if (length(hk_vals) == 0L) {
    append_sanity(
      sprintf("housekeeping_cv_%s", hk_symbol),
      "WARN",
      NA_real_,
      0.3,
      sprintf("%s (%s) not found in gene_expression_normalised_%s.csv.gz", hk_symbol, hk_id, tf)
    )
    next
  }
  hk_cv <- sd(hk_vals, na.rm = TRUE) / mean(hk_vals, na.rm = TRUE)
  append_sanity(
    sprintf("housekeeping_cv_%s", hk_symbol),
    ifelse(hk_cv < 0.3, "PASS", "WARN"),
    hk_cv,
    0.3,
    sprintf("cross-sample CV of gene_expression_getmm for %s (%s); expect < 0.3", hk_symbol, hk_id)
  )
}

# 4. §4.12e VST-gate CHECK (was a mask; masking now happens upstream in
# 02-3-rmats-event-filtering.Rmd). Verify every surviving (event,sample) row
# has host-gene VST at/above the cutoff 02-3 recorded — i.e. the upstream gate
# held. Rows with NA VST are allowed under the 'keep' NA policy. This is a
# check, not a mask: it must never mutate aggregated_dt.
vst_cutoff_file <- sprintf("qc/vst_expression_cutoff_%s.csv", tf)
if (file.exists(vst_cutoff_file)) {
  vst_cutoff_dt <- fread(vst_cutoff_file)
  vst_cutoff_val <- vst_cutoff_dt$cutoff[1]
  na_policy <- getOption("EpiATLAS_AS_VST_NA_POLICY", "keep")
  viol <- aggregated_dt[
    !is.na(gene_expression_vst) & gene_expression_vst < vst_cutoff_val,
    .N
  ]
  frac_viol <- viol / max(1L, nrow(aggregated_dt))
  append_sanity(
    "vst_gate_upstream_held",
    if (frac_viol < 1e-6) "PASS" else "FAIL",
    frac_viol,
    vst_cutoff_val,
    sprintf(
      "fraction of surviving rows with vst < cutoff (should be 0; gate in 02-3; na_policy=%s)",
      na_policy
    )
  )
} else {
  append_sanity(
    "vst_gate_upstream_held",
    "WARN",
    NA_real_,
    NA_real_,
    sprintf("%s not found — cannot verify upstream VST gate", vst_cutoff_file)
  )
}
```


```{r, junction-coverage-sanity}
# §4.13i — junction read coverage. The per-(event,sample) read-coverage gate is
# now APPLIED UPSTREAM in 02-3 (expr_pass: cells with IJC+SJC < min_read_coverage
# are masked to NA PSI and dropped from the .jc file; NA-PSI rows are dropped here
# at load). So every surviving cell already clears the floor — this is no longer a
# DISCOVERY check but a VERIFICATION that the gate propagated 02-3 → 03 → 05
# (a below-floor cell here would mean a .psi/.jc desync or a stale input).

# Distribution is still informative: it now shows the POST-gate coverage, with a
# hard left edge at the cutoff.
min_read_coverage <- getOption("EpiATLAS_AS_MIN_READ_COVERAGE", 10)
p_junction_cov <- ggplot(aggregated_dt, aes(x = log10(IJC + SJC + 1))) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 50, fill = "steelblue", color = "white") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = log10(min_read_coverage + 1), linetype = "dashed", colour = "red") +
  facet_wrap(~`Event Type`, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(
    title = sprintf("Post-gate junction coverage (floor = %d reads)", min_read_coverage),
    subtitle = "dashed = applied per-cell gate (02-3 expr_pass)",
    x = "log10(IJC + SJC + 1)"
  )
print(p_junction_cov)
ggsave(
  "qc/distributions/junction_coverage.pdf",
  p_junction_cov,
  width = 9,
  height = 5
)

# Gate-held verification: NO surviving cell may fall below the upstream floor.
cov_cells <- aggregated_dt[!is.na(IJC) & !is.na(SJC)]
min_cell_cov <- cov_cells[, min(IJC + SJC)]
n_below <- cov_cells[IJC + SJC < min_read_coverage, .N]
append_sanity(
  "junction_coverage_gate_held",
  ifelse(n_below == 0L, "PASS", "FAIL"),
  min_cell_cov,
  min_read_coverage,
  sprintf(
    "min IJC+SJC over surviving cells = %g (upstream 02-3 gate = %d); %d cells below (want 0)",
    min_cell_cov, min_read_coverage, n_below
  )
)
```

```{r, ri-protocol-sanity}
# §4.13k — 05 now builds ONE transcript_filter per run, so no cross-filter loop
# (aggregated_dt holds a single filter `tf`). Check the known RI PSI~protocol
# bias (total-RNA-Seq inflates RI PSI by ~0.05 vs mRNA-Seq) isn't concentrated in
# specific ontologies. An ontology sampled almost entirely by one protocol would
# let protocol bias masquerade as a genuine tissue effect downstream, since
# protocol and ontology become statistically inseparable in that subgroup.
#
# Two things actually need showing here, and neither is "residuals from
# lm(PSI~protocol)" (tried first, dropped): that shows leftover PSI variance with
# the protocol effect removed, which is bounded/skewed and not what a confound
# check needs to see.
#  1. sample composition per ontology (the confound itself: is one protocol
#     dominant?).
#  2. the protocol effect size per ontology (does the known ~0.05 bias hold
#     everywhere, or blow up in specific tissues?).
ri_dt <- aggregated_dt[`Event Type` == "RI"]

# --- 1. protocol composition per ontology ---------------------------------
protocol_composition <- unique(
  ri_dt[, .(uuid, ontology, protocol)]
)[, .N, by = .(ontology, protocol)]

p_protocol_composition <- ggplot(
  protocol_composition,
  aes(x = ontology, y = N, fill = protocol)
) +
  geom_col(position = "fill") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.5, linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(
    title = sprintf("RNA-Seq protocol composition by ontology (%s)", tf),
    x = "ontology",
    y = "fraction of samples"
  ) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 1, vjust = 0.5))
print(p_protocol_composition)
ggsave(
  sprintf("qc/distributions/protocol_composition_by_ontology_%s.pdf", tf),
  p_protocol_composition,
  width = 9,
  height = 5
)

# --- 2. protocol effect size (total-RNA-Seq - mRNA-Seq) per ontology ------
# single-protocol ontologies (no contrast) get NA_real_; type-consistent so the
# by-group bind doesn't hit an int/double mismatch. PSI now carries VST-masked
# NAs, so drop them before the effect estimate.
protocol_effect <- ri_dt[,
  {
    psi_total <- PSI[protocol == "total-RNA-Seq" & !is.na(PSI)]
    psi_mrna <- PSI[protocol == "mRNA-Seq" & !is.na(PSI)]
    if (length(psi_total) < 2L || length(psi_mrna) < 2L) {
      list(
        effect = NA_real_,
        ci_lo = NA_real_,
        ci_hi = NA_real_,
        n_samples = uniqueN(uuid)
      )
    } else {
      effect <- mean(psi_total) - mean(psi_mrna)
      se <- sqrt(
        var(psi_total) / length(psi_total) + var(psi_mrna) / length(psi_mrna)
      )
      list(
        effect = effect,
        ci_lo = effect - 1.96 * se,
        ci_hi = effect + 1.96 * se,
        n_samples = uniqueN(uuid)
      )
    }
  },
  by = .(ontology)
]

p_protocol_effect <- ggplot(
  protocol_effect,
  aes(x = ontology, y = effect, ymin = ci_lo, ymax = ci_hi)
) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "solid", color = "grey50") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.05, linetype = "dashed", color = "red") +
  geom_pointrange() +
  labs(
    title = sprintf(
      "RI PSI protocol effect (total-RNA-Seq - mRNA-Seq) by ontology (%s)",
      tf
    ),
    subtitle = "dashed red line = known global bias (~0.05)",
    x = "ontology",
    y = "mean PSI difference"
  ) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 1, vjust = 0.5))
print(p_protocol_effect)
ggsave(
  sprintf("qc/distributions/ri_protocol_effect_by_ontology_%s.pdf", tf),
  p_protocol_effect,
  width = 9,
  height = 5
)

# flag ontologies where one protocol accounts for > 50% of samples (among
# ontologies with > 50 samples total, per spec) — below that size a
# single-protocol skew is expected sampling noise, not a real confound
protocol_balance <- protocol_composition[,
  .(max_frac = max(N) / sum(N), n_samples = sum(N)),
  by = ontology
]
confounded_ontologies <- protocol_balance[
  max_frac > 0.5 & n_samples > 50,
  ontology
]
append_sanity(
  sprintf("ri_protocol_ontology_confound_%s", tf),
  ifelse(length(confounded_ontologies) == 0, "PASS", "WARN"),
  length(confounded_ontologies),
  0,
  paste("confounded ontologies:", paste(confounded_ontologies, collapse = ", "))
)
```


```{r, join-maxentscan}
# §4.13e — MaxEntScan splice-site scores (written by maxentscan_scores rule).
# Score files are row-order-aligned with their source FASTA; IDs come from
# the FASTA headers (">ID").
scores3 <- fread(
  sprintf("processed_data/3scores_%s.txt", tf),
  col.names = c("sequence", "3ss")
)
scores3down <- fread(
  sprintf("processed_data/3down_scores_%s.txt", tf),
  col.names = c("sequence", "3ssdown")
)
scores5 <- fread(
  sprintf("processed_data/5scores_%s.txt", tf),
  col.names = c("sequence", "5ss")
)
scores5up <- fread(
  sprintf("processed_data/5up_scores_%s.txt", tf),
  col.names = c("sequence", "5ssup")
)

scores3[,
  ID := as.integer(substr(
    grep(
      "^>",
      readLines(sprintf("processed_data/3ss_%s.fasta", tf)),
      value = TRUE
    ),
    2,
    .Machine$integer.max
  ))
]
scores5[,
  ID := as.integer(substr(
    grep(
      "^>",
      readLines(sprintf("processed_data/5ss_%s.fasta", tf)),
      value = TRUE
    ),
    2,
    .Machine$integer.max
  ))
]
scores3[, `3ssdown` := scores3down[["3ssdown"]]]
scores5[, `5ssup` := scores5up[["5ssup"]]]
scores3[, sequence := NULL]
scores5[, sequence := NULL]
ss_dt <- merge(scores3, scores5, by = "ID", all = TRUE)

ss_cols <- c("3ss", "3ssdown", "5ss", "5ssup")
aggregated_dt[ss_dt, on = .(ID), (ss_cols) := mget(paste0("i.", ss_cols))]

# sanity: distributions + NA fraction
dir.create("qc/distributions", recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
ss_cols <- c("3ss", "3ssdown", "5ss", "5ssup")
# scores are per-event (constant across all sample rows sharing an ID), so
# dedupe on (ID, transcript_filter) before plotting - otherwise the
# histogram would be weighted by per-event sample count rather than by
# event, and that weighting differs across transcript_filter/Event Type.
ss_plot_cols <- c("ID", ss_cols, "Event Type", "transcript_filter")
ss_dedup <- unique(
  aggregated_dt[, ..ss_plot_cols],
  by = c("ID", "transcript_filter")
)
ss_long <- melt(
  ss_dedup,
  id.vars = c("Event Type", "transcript_filter"),
  measure.vars = ss_cols,
  variable.name = "site",
  value.name = "score"
)
ss_long[, site := factor(site, levels = c('5ssup', '3ss', '5ss', '3ssdown'))]
p_splice_scores <- ggplot(ss_long, aes(x = score)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 50, fill = "steelblue", color = "white") +
  facet_wrap(site ~ `Event Type`, scales = "free_y", ncol = 2) +
  labs(title = "MaxEntScan score distributions", x = "score")
print(p_splice_scores)
ggsave(
  "qc/distributions/splice_site_scores.pdf",
  p_splice_scores,
  width = 12,
  height = 14
)
ss_na_frac <- aggregated_dt[, mean(
  is.na(`3ss`) | is.na(`3ssdown`) | is.na(`5ss`) | is.na(`5ssup`)
)]
stopifnot(ss_na_frac < 0.01)
append_sanity(
  sprintf("splice_site_na_frac__%s", tf),
  if (ss_na_frac < 0.01) "PASS" else "FAIL",
  ss_na_frac,
  0.01,
  "NA fraction across the 4 MaxEntScan score columns"
)

# §4.13e — score-distribution sanity (per-event, deduped). Expected ranges
# (Yeo & Burge MaxEntScan): 5'ss ~[-20,12] median ~8; 3'ss ~[-30,16] median ~8.
# Median well below these floors => coordinate/strand or frame bug.
for (col in ss_cols) {
  med <- ss_dedup[, median(get(col), na.rm = TRUE)]
  lo <- if (startsWith(col, "5")) -20 else -30
  hi <- if (startsWith(col, "5")) 12 else 16
  in_range <- ss_dedup[, mean(get(col) >= lo & get(col) <= hi, na.rm = TRUE)]
  append_sanity(
    sprintf("splice_site_median_%s__%s", col, tf),
    if (med > 0) "PASS" else "WARN",
    med,
    0,
    sprintf(
      "median %s score (Yeo-Burge expects ~8; range [%d,%d], %.1f%% in range)",
      col,
      lo,
      hi,
      100 * in_range
    )
  )
}

# §4.13e — RI splice sites should be WEAKER than SE (weak 5'/3' sites are a
# primary driver of intron retention). Compare median 5ss+3ss by Event Type.
if (uniqueN(ss_dedup$`Event Type`) > 1) {
  ss_strength <- ss_dedup[,
    .(
      strength = median(`5ss` + `3ss`, na.rm = TRUE)
    ),
    by = `Event Type`
  ]
  ri_str <- ss_strength[`Event Type` == "RI", strength]
  se_str <- ss_strength[`Event Type` == "SE", strength]
  if (length(ri_str) && length(se_str)) {
    append_sanity(
      sprintf("splice_site_ri_weaker_than_se__%s", tf),
      if (ri_str < se_str) "PASS" else "WARN",
      ri_str - se_str,
      0,
      sprintf(
        "median(5ss+3ss): RI=%.2f SE=%.2f (RI should be lower)",
        ri_str,
        se_str
      )
    )
  }
}
```


```{r, join-pangolin}
# §4.13e-ext — Pangolin splice-site usage scores (written by pangolin_scores
# rule). Guarded: rule may not have finished yet.
pangolin_scores_file <- sprintf("processed_data/pangolin_scores_%s.csv", tf)
if (file.exists(pangolin_scores_file)) {
  pangolin_raw <- fread(pangolin_scores_file)
  # Map each Pangolin site_type to the SAME four splice-site positions
  # MaxEntScan uses (5ss / 5ssup / 3ss / 3ssdown) — NOT a 2-way donor/acceptor
  # collapse. Averaging the two donors (or the two/three acceptors) together
  # blurs distinct sites that 03 scores separately; the two tools must line up
  # position-for-position. Coordinate correspondence (03 fasta export):
  #   5ss     = alt/skipped-exon donor (E2)   = alt_donor  / (RI) donor
  #   5ssup   = upstream-exon donor    (E1)   = upstream_donor
  #   3ss     = alt/skipped-exon acceptor(E2) = alt_acceptor / (RI) acceptor
  #   3ssdown = downstream-exon acceptor (E3) = downstream_acceptor
  # RI has only donor+acceptor, so pangolin_5ssup/3ssdown are NA for RI events
  # (Pangolin scores no separate upstream/downstream site there).
  pangolin_raw[,
    ss_pos := fcase(
      site_type %in% c("alt_donor", "donor"),       "5ss",
      site_type == "upstream_donor",                "5ssup",
      site_type %in% c("alt_acceptor", "acceptor"), "3ss",
      site_type == "downstream_acceptor",           "3ssdown",
      default = NA_character_
    )
  ]
  # 04-4 emits TWO quantities per tissue (schema 2026-07-09):
  #   psite = P(splice site) — sequence-intrinsic site STRENGTH (MaxEntScan-analog)
  #   usage = tissue-specific predicted splicing level ∈[0,1] — PSI-comparable
  # Carry both (+ their across-tissue CV). Each (event_id, ss_pos) is one row here
  # (each site_type maps to one position); mean() is a safe passthrough.
  pangolin_agg <- pangolin_raw[
    !is.na(ss_pos),
    .(
      psite_mean = mean(psite_mean, na.rm = TRUE),
      psite_cv   = mean(psite_tissue_cv, na.rm = TRUE),
      usage_mean = mean(usage_mean, na.rm = TRUE),
      usage_cv   = mean(usage_tissue_cv, na.rm = TRUE)
    ),
    by = .(event_id, ss_pos)
  ]
  # wide: one row per event; dcast names cols "<val>_<pos>" (e.g. psite_mean_5ss),
  # rename to pangolin_<pos>_<val> (pangolin_5ss_psite_mean, pangolin_5ss_usage_mean, …)
  pangolin_wide <- dcast(
    pangolin_agg,
    event_id ~ ss_pos,
    value.var = c("psite_mean", "psite_cv", "usage_mean", "usage_cv")
  )
  old_names <- setdiff(names(pangolin_wide), "event_id")
  setnames(
    pangolin_wide,
    old_names,
    sub("^(psite_mean|psite_cv|usage_mean|usage_cv)_(.+)$", "pangolin_\\2_\\1", old_names)
  )

  id_map <- unique(event_annotations_dt[, .(event_id, ID)])
  pangolin_dt <- id_map[pangolin_wide, on = .(event_id)]
  pangolin_cols <- setdiff(names(pangolin_dt), c("event_id", "ID"))
  aggregated_dt[
    pangolin_dt,
    on = .(ID),
    (pangolin_cols) := mget(paste0("i.", pangolin_cols))
  ]

  # concordance PER EVENT TYPE: SE and RI have different site sets (RI has no
  # upstream_donor/downstream_acceptor, so its 5ssup/3ssdown are NA) and are best
  # checked separately. For each (event_type, site): MaxEntScan score vs Pangolin
  # P(splice) at the SAME position — both score site STRENGTH, so Spearman r should
  # be positive; low/negative => coord/join mismatch there. Uses psite (not usage):
  # P(splice) is the sharp positional signal (~0.8 at a correct site, ~0.05 one base
  # off), so it cleanly flags a coordinate error (this is how the donor-offset bug
  # surfaced as −0.42). A site absent for a type (n<2 pairs) is INFO, not WARN.
  # SE 5ss (alt-exon donor) is the primary coord-alignment gate (hard stopifnot).
  ss_pangolin_map <- c(
    `5ss`     = "pangolin_5ss_psite_mean",
    `5ssup`   = "pangolin_5ssup_psite_mean",
    `3ss`     = "pangolin_3ss_psite_mean",
    `3ssdown` = "pangolin_3ssdown_psite_mean"
  )
  dedup_ss <- aggregated_dt[!duplicated(ID)]
  for (et in dedup_ss[, unique(`Event Type`)]) {
    sub_et <- dedup_ss[`Event Type` == et]
    for (mss in names(ss_pangolin_map)) {
      pcol <- ss_pangolin_map[[mss]]
      n_pair <- sub_et[!is.na(get(mss)) & !is.na(get(pcol)), .N]
      r <- if (n_pair >= 2L) {
        cor(sub_et[[mss]], sub_et[[pcol]], method = "spearman", use = "complete.obs")
      } else {
        NA_real_
      }
      cat(sprintf("[%s] Spearman r(%s, %s) = %.3f  (n=%d)\n", et, mss, pcol, r, n_pair))
      append_sanity(
        sprintf("pangolin_maxentscan_concordance_%s_%s__%s", et, mss, tf),
        if (n_pair < 2L) "INFO" else if (r > 0.2) "PASS" else "WARN", r, 0.2,
        sprintf("%s: Spearman r(MaxEntScan %s, %s), n=%d; same site, expect > 0.2", et, mss, pcol, n_pair)
      )
      append_sanity(
        sprintf("pangolin_%s_%s_na_frac__%s", et, mss, tf),
        "INFO", sub_et[, mean(is.na(get(pcol)))], NA_real_,
        sprintf("%s: fraction with no Pangolin %s score (RI has none for 5ssup/3ssdown)", et, mss)
      )
    }
  }
  # primary coord-alignment gate: SE alt-exon donor must concord
  se_ss <- dedup_ss[`Event Type` == "SE"]
  cor_5ss_pangolin <- cor(
    se_ss$`5ss`, se_ss$pangolin_5ss_psite_mean,
    method = "spearman", use = "complete.obs"
  )
  stopifnot(cor_5ss_pangolin > 0.2)
} else {
  warning(sprintf(
    "%s not found — skipping Pangolin join (§4.13e-ext)",
    pangolin_scores_file
  ))
  append_sanity(
    sprintf("pangolin_join__%s", tf),
    "WARN",
    NA_real_,
    NA_real_,
    sprintf("%s absent — Pangolin columns not joined", pangolin_scores_file)
  )
}
```


```{r, dnam-tss-sanity}
# §4.13c item 3 — DNAm β vs TSS proximity. Lives here (not 04-1): distance_TSS
# is an event annotation that only exists after the 05 join. Biology: promoter/
# TSS-proximal regions are hypomethylated, gene-body/intergenic hypermethylated,
# so mean β should RISE with distance_TSS. Reported as INFO (Spearman r + a
# per-bin boxplot) rather than a hard PASS/WARN: the sign depends on how
# distance_TSS is defined (the §4.13c prose and this biology disagree on sign),
# so we surface the value + plot and let it be read, not assert a direction.
dnam_cols <- grep("^DNAm;", names(aggregated_dt), value = TRUE)
if (length(dnam_cols) && "distance_TSS" %in% names(aggregated_dt)) {
  ev_beta <- aggregated_dt[, c("ID", "distance_TSS", dnam_cols), with = FALSE]
  ev_beta[, beta_row := rowMeans(.SD, na.rm = TRUE), .SDcols = dnam_cols]
  ev_agg <- ev_beta[,
    .(
      beta = mean(beta_row, na.rm = TRUE),
      distance_TSS = distance_TSS[1]
    ),
    by = ID
  ]
  ev_agg <- ev_agg[is.finite(beta) & is.finite(distance_TSS)]
  r_tss <- ev_agg[, cor(
    beta,
    log10(distance_TSS + 1),
    method = "spearman",
    use = "complete.obs"
  )]
  cat(sprintf("Spearman(mean beta, log10(distance_TSS+1)) = %.3f\n", r_tss))
  append_sanity(
    sprintf("dnam_beta_vs_tss__%s", tf),
    "INFO",
    r_tss,
    NA_real_,
    "Spearman(mean beta, log10(distance_TSS+1)); expect TSS-proximal hypomethylated"
  )
  ev_agg[,
    tss_bin := cut(
      distance_TSS,
      breaks = c(-Inf, 1e3, 5e3, 1e4, 5e4, Inf),
      labels = c("0-1kb", "1-5kb", "5-10kb", "10-50kb", ">50kb")
    )
  ]
  p_tss <- ggplot(ev_agg[!is.na(tss_bin)], aes(tss_bin, beta)) +
    geom_boxplot(fill = "steelblue", outlier.size = 0.3) +
    labs(
      title = sprintf("DNAm vs TSS distance (%s)", tf),
      subtitle = sprintf(
        "per-event mean beta across samples x DNAm windows; Spearman r = %.3f",
        r_tss
      ),
      x = "distance to TSS",
      y = "mean beta (% methylation)"
    )
  print(p_tss)
  ggsave(
    sprintf("qc/distributions/dnam_beta_vs_tss_%s.pdf", tf),
    p_tss,
    width = 7,
    height = 5
  )
}
```

```{r, gene-expression-by-event-type}
# Relocated here from 02-2-rnaseq-normalisation.Rmd (which now runs before 03
# and so cannot see event annotations). Genome-wide gene expression by hosted
# event type: are SE/RI-hosting genes expressed differently from the
# background of all genes? Uses the full per-filter normalisation table (all
# genes, from gene_quants_agg) classified by which event type(s) each gene
# hosts (from event_annotations_dt) — event-hosting genes vs a
# "No annotated event" reference category.
gene_event_types <- event_annotations_dt[,
  .(
    has_se = any(`Event Type` == "SE"),
    has_ri = any(`Event Type` == "RI")
  ),
  by = .(gene_id)
]
gene_event_types[,
  event_type_class := fcase(
    has_se & has_ri , "Both"    ,
    has_se          , "SE only" ,
    has_ri          , "RI only"
  )
]
gene_event_types[, gene_id_stripped := gsub("\\.\\d+$", "", gene_id)]

gene_median_expr <- gene_quants_agg[,
  .(
    median_getmm = median(gene_expression_getmm, na.rm = TRUE),
    median_vst = median(gene_expression_vst, na.rm = TRUE)
  ),
  by = .(gene_id)
]
gene_median_expr[, gene_id_stripped := gsub("\\.\\d+$", "", gene_id)]
# update-join keeps ALL genes; event_type_class NA for non-event-hosting genes
gene_median_expr[
  gene_event_types,
  on = .(gene_id_stripped),
  event_type_class := i.event_type_class
]
gene_median_expr[
  is.na(event_type_class),
  event_type_class := "No annotated event"
]
gene_median_expr[,
  event_type_class := factor(
    event_type_class,
    levels = c("No annotated event", "SE only", "RI only", "Both")
  )
]

dir.create("qc/distributions", recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
p_getmm_et <- ggplot(
  gene_median_expr,
  aes(x = event_type_class, y = log1p(median_getmm), fill = event_type_class)
) +
  geom_violin(trim = FALSE, alpha = 0.6, linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_boxplot(width = 0.15, outlier.shape = NA, alpha = 0.9, linewidth = 0.3) +
  scale_fill_viridis_d(option = "D", guide = "none") +
  labs(
    title = sprintf("Gene GeTMM-CPM by hosted event type (%s)", tf),
    subtitle = "per-gene median across samples, log1p",
    x = NULL,
    y = "log1p(GeTMM-CPM)"
  ) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1))
print(p_getmm_et)
ggsave(
  sprintf("qc/distributions/gene_expression_getmm_by_event_type_%s.pdf", tf),
  p_getmm_et,
  width = 6,
  height = 5
)

p_vst_et <- ggplot(
  gene_median_expr,
  aes(x = event_type_class, y = median_vst, fill = event_type_class)
) +
  geom_violin(trim = FALSE, alpha = 0.6, linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_boxplot(width = 0.15, outlier.shape = NA, alpha = 0.9, linewidth = 0.3) +
  scale_fill_viridis_d(option = "D", guide = "none") +
  labs(
    title = sprintf("Gene vst by hosted event type (%s)", tf),
    subtitle = "per-gene median across samples (vst: no further transform)",
    x = NULL,
    y = "vst(expression)"
  ) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1))
print(p_vst_et)
ggsave(
  sprintf("qc/distributions/gene_expression_vst_by_event_type_%s.pdf", tf),
  p_vst_et,
  width = 6,
  height = 5
)
```
